description: Compare dividend reinvesting (DRIP) vs taking cash payouts on long-term growth, with dividend growth compounding.

faqs.a: With DRIP, each dividend buys more shares, so the next dividend is larger — compounding on compounding. Cash payouts keep the share count fixed.
Each year the dividend yield applies to the current value, and the yield itself grows by the dividend-growth rate you enter.
faqs.q: What is dividend growth in this model?

faqs.a: Higher yield with high growth and long horizons favors DRIP most; over decades the gap can be several multiples.
faqs.q: When does DRIP make the biggest difference?

howto: Enter the initial investment, dividend yield and dividend growth rate.
Set the time horizon and toggle DRIP on or off.
Compare ending values side by side.
title: Dividend Reinvestment Calculator
